utterances.text: The strategy should recognize these contributions when measuring housing growth and more actively promote rehab and adaptive reuse as alternatives to mass demolition and displacement.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next, we'll hear from Christina Farabazina.

chapters.summary: She supports Block by Block but wants comprehensive neighborhood plan, deep affordability, community ownership, dedicated funds for community land trusts, and anti-displacement protections.
chapters.title: Christina Weggs testifies on community ownership and anti-displacement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: Hi, thanks so much for having us today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: My name's Christina Weggs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: I'm an independent consultant, and I work on justice-focused urban policy, community co-design, and participatory governance of urban development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: I live in Kensington Flatbush, which is part of the south of Prospect Plan area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: And like we've heard from many of us here, me and my neighbors, we support block to block, but we think it must be delivered through a comprehensive neighborhood plan, just as you've reiterated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: I agree with many of the points that have been made, so maybe I'll add a few more on the table.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: I think as a resident and as a practitioner, my interest is to ensure that long-time residents and local businesses in my neighborhood can both shape the growth that's coming to our neighborhood and benefit from that growth rather than being displaced from it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: And I have four asks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: One, and I think we heard very eloquently from others, we need deep and meaningful affordability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: Every rezone area and city-owned site should report on how many new homes are affordable at the 30 and 50 percent of area median income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: And we should set targets for each community district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: Also, as you reiterated yourself, we really need pathways to community ownership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: Ownership lets the community members stay and share in the value that growth is creating in their neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: And I'm asking, and we heard a little bit about this, for dedicated funds with technical support for community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: land trust, co-ops, tenants in small buildings, and affordable ground floor space for local businesses on city sites.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: We need meaningful community engagement throughout the whole process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: I'm very grateful that in my area, council members Rita Joseph, Shana Hanif, and Farrah Lewis, as well as the city department, have the city planning department have already started great engagement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: I'm asking that that continue not just through our 2027 plan, but throughout construction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: And what I heard in a meeting yesterday was the critical importance of funding local groups who are able to continuously convene community members who might not be reached by the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: A draft plan should show how it reflected and responded to what community members asked for, and there needs to be a public tracker and a local advisory group to track that commitments are followed through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: The last point I'd like to make, and I'll add this, is we need anti-displacement protections before rezoning and transit arrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christina Weggs
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Sayonara.

chapters.summary: She asks how Block by Block fits with other strategies, how it works in dense neighborhoods, and calls for preservation of existing affordable housing and replacement of demolished units.
chapters.title: Zeynep Turan of Friends of Upper East Side testifies on preservation and deep affordability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: Hi, Chair Riley.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: My name is Zeynep Turan, and I'm here on behalf of Friends of the Upper East Side, a leading voice for common sense development since 1982.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: Friends supports housing equity and recognizes New York City's urgent need for affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: We applaud Block by Block's ambitious 10-year target of adding 200,000 new affordable homes and the commitment to preserve more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: But we have three questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: First, how does Block by Block fit into the city's broader housing strategy?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: How will it coordinate with City of Yes Housing Opportunity and the Fair Housing Strategy to avoid overlapping targets, measure combined results, and ensure accountability?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: Echoing Council Member Brewer and her frustration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: Second, we ask, how will this plan work in the city's densest neighborhoods, where underutilized land is scarce?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: On the Upper East Side, particularly in Yorkville, low-rise multifamily buildings with rent-stabilized apartments are being replaced by luxury condominiums with zero affordable housing units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: How will block-by-block plan address this loss?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: Success cannot be measured only by new homes built, but also must factor in affordable homes lost.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: And to that end, between 2008 and 2025, Community District 8, our district, lost 14,793 rents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: stabilized apartments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: This makes preservation of existing affordable housing essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: France calls on the city to require developers demolishing buildings with affordable apartments to replace every affordable unit demolished with an equivalent affordable unit built on site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: Third, how will the city preserve existing affordability, support landlords, and deliver deeper affordability on the Upper East Side?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: And what specific measures will bring deeper affordability to the Upper East Side, a neighborhood that is increasingly becoming high cost for the low-income residents?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: In conclusion, we urge the city to make preservation, deep affordability, and neighborhood-specific solutions central to this plan with an adequate public review process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zeynep Turan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Our next panel will consist of Dan Fortini, Anthony Orlowski, sorry for mispronouncing his name, Matthew Guliata, and Dave Parney.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We'll begin first with Dan, followed by Anthony, Matthew, then Dave.

chapters.summary: He opposes expansion of plastic piping in buildings taller than five stories, says it poses fire safety and public health risks, and asks for public disclosure of task force recommendations.
chapters.title: Dan Fortini of Plumbers Local 1 testifies on plastic piping opposition

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Chair Riley and members of the committee, my name is Dan Fortini, and I'm a proud member of Plumbers Local Union number one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: I also serve on the Plumbing Technical Code Committee alongside Paul O'Connor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: He's the business manager of Local One, and today I have the privilege of presenting testimony on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: For generations, our members have built and maintained the critical plumbing infrastructure

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: that delivers safe drinking water, removes wastewater, and protects the health and safety of millions of New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Let me be unmistakably clear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Local One supports building more housing that working families can afford, but the housing crisis is not a blank check to weaken public safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: We reject the false choice between affordability and safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: And New Yorkers deserve both.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: We unequivocally oppose the use and expansion of plastic piping in all capacities, including PEX.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: This is not an opening bid for compromise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Reducing construction costs cannot justify transferring risks to residents, building operators, or firefighters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: The administration cannot use the block-by-block housing plan

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: to bypass the established construction code committee process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: The affordable and efficient code reform task force cannot become a vehicle for reviving rejected proposals behind closed doors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: New York City's density and building standards

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: stock demand local scrutiny, not shortcuts dressed up as reform.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: The council should demand public disclosure of the task force's membership, recommendations, supporting evidence, and dissenting views.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: FDNY participation is essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Contemplating changes involving combustible materials without the firefighters to respond when systems fail is indefensible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Fire safety is not negotiable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Plastic piping systems can soften, melt, or burn, and the consequences of this extends beyond the failed pipe to residents and emergency responders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Before expanding plastic piping, the city should subject fire performance and the integrity of affected fire stopping systems to independent technical review.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Public health demands scrutiny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Concerns about plastic piping, biofilm, and safe disinfection require independent examination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: That review needs to address Legionnaire's disease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: The city has a responsibility to demonstrate that proposed systems can safely be maintained and remediated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Testimony has been submitted and written.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Fortini
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you, Dan.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Anthony?

chapters.summary: He opposes plastic piping in tall buildings, says it is inferior to cast iron and copper, and performance depends on installation quality.
chapters.title: Anthony Orlowski of McWane Plumbing Group testifies on plastic piping

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: My name is Anthony Orlowski.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: I'm executive vice president of McWane Plumbing Group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: McWane is a leading U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: Manufacturer of plumbing and water infrastructure products, including cast iron pipe and fittings that are used in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: I'm here today to express McWane's strong opposition to this plan's proposal to expand the use of plastic piping in buildings taller than five stories.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: As this committee knows, building codes are established for the purpose of protecting the public, ultimately from health and safety hazards, but first and foremost from the bad decisions that otherwise might lead to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: It is always a wrong decision to trade someone's safety for anything else, even if done with the best of intentions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: And no code should be changed that it results in worse health and safety outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: Plastic piping is at its best inferior to cast iron and copper in health and safety performance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: That's at its best.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: And while the high performance of cast iron and copper are inherent to the materials themselves, I'd like to remind the committee that the performance of plastic is dependent on the quality of the installation and its supporting systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: Absent 100% inspection by a third party,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: Someone installing plastic systems with the goal of cost reduction will be pressured to take shortcuts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: This takes inferior performance and reduces it to unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: New York City can advance affordable housing while maintaining the fire safety and public health standards that protect its residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: All New Yorkers deserve plumbing systems that are safe, reliable, and built to last.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Orlowski
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you, Matthew.

chapters.summary: He says the housing plan will increase workloads for inspectors at DOB, HPD, and NYCHA, and asks for increased funding for inspector staffing and equipment.
chapters.title: Matthew Gagliotta of Allied Building Inspectors Local 211 testifies on inspector staffing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Chairman, members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: My name is Matthew Gagliotta, President and Business Manager of Allied Building Inspectors, Local 211, International Union of Operating Engineers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Local 211 represents New York City's building and housing inspectors employed at the three agencies that will play a significant role in implementing this housing plan, Department of Buildings, HPD, and NYCHA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Our members'workloads will be directly impacted and significantly increased by this plan across all agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: While our members are certainly up to the challenge, and we support any housing plan that will address our city's housing crisis, will this plan and this council take into account

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: The critical need to increase funding for inspector staffing levels across all inspector titles at all three agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Address decades-long recruitment and retention issues of inspectors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Provide adequate equipment to carry out our enforcement and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: In order for any housing plant to succeed, there must be robust housing maintenance code enforcement, construction safety compliance inspections,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: as well as construction development that is zoning resolution and code compliant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Inspector staffing levels must be addressed for any plan to succeed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Our members take great pride in ensuring public safety and ensuring tenants have the dignified, safe housing that they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: We look forward to being on the front lines of the housing crisis and carrying out our duties, whether at DOB, HBD, or NYCHA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Gagliotta
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you, Dave.

chapters.summary: He opposes plastic piping in buildings taller than five stories, cites fire safety and water safety concerns, and urges council to oppose code changes.
chapters.title: Dave Parney of Cast Iron Soil Pipe Institute testifies on plastic piping

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Riley and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: My name is Dave Parney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: I'm the Executive Vice President of the Cast Iron Soil Pipe Institute, or CISPE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Founded in 1949, CISPE represents U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Manufacturers of cast iron soil pipe and fittings used in the building construction for drain waste and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: vent plumbing systems here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: I'm here to express CISPE's strong opposition to a proposal in the block-by-block plan to expand the use of plastic piping in buildings taller than five stories.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: On page 99 of this block-by-block program, the plan calls for a Department of Buildings task force to identify code changes that could reduce housing costs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: One proposal is to permit plastic piping in taller buildings based on its lower material cost.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: However, New York City has restricted plastics use in these buildings for more than 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: And similar restrictions exist nationwide due to significant safety concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: We support building more affordable housing, but affordable housing must never come at the expense of fire safety or public health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: I'll explain some of these issues in brief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: First, fire safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Plastic piping will melt, burn, and produce smoke during a fire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: These systems also depend on fire stop devices at wall and floor penetrations to prevent fire and smoke from spreading through the building and causing health and safety concerns to the residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Once concealed, these devices can be difficult to inspect and maintain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Second, water safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Research has raised concerns of biofilm growth, Legionella bacteria in plastic pipings, inability to withstand disinfection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Independent studies have found Legionella more frequently in systems using plastic piping than those using copper, raising serious public health concerns about expanding its use in larger residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Finally, CISPI urges the Council oppose any code changes that would expand plastic piping's use in buildings taller than five stories.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: New Yorkers deserve safe, reliable plumbing, and affordable housing must never mean compromising the safety of the people who live in it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Parney
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify, and I'm happy to answer any questions.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: For your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This is Pound's excuse.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next, we're going to hear from Ron.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And can you guys please submit those testimonies to us as well?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Rhonda Wiss, John Biggers, and Patricia Legate.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If there's anyone else that has signed up to testify, please see the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Following this testimony, we're going to go into a virtual panel.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: That virtual panel is going to consist of...

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Kyle Ems, Cheryl Mervin, and Dominic Duriski.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: That will be the virtual panel after this.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yes, I did call you Patricia.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Maybe I mispronounced your name.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: John, and is Rhonda here?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Rhonda Wiss?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We'll start with Patricia, then followed by John.

utterances.text: I'm here on a very important matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate
utterances.text: My life almost was taken from me due to a fraud that I discovered in where I live, which is Rosedale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate
utterances.text: So I was so disturbed by it, but I needed a place to stay because I become homeless with my kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate
utterances.text: I fixed the property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate
utterances.text: And with my money, even appliances, I put all the appliances that was, my house was taken into the apartment and I move in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate
utterances.text: As I move in,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patricia Legate

chapters.summary: He opposes plastic piping in tall buildings, cites fire safety concerns, and says height restrictions are common nationwide.
chapters.title: John Biggers of Charlotte Pipe and Foundry testifies on plastic piping

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: That's tough to follow there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Chair Riley, thank you so much for allowing me to be here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: My name is John Biggers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: I am president of Charlotte Pipe and Foundry Company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: During my 37 years at Charlotte Pipe, I've covered New York City for 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: And I'm intimately familiar with the plumbing systems in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Matter of fact, we might be able to help the lady with her TNP valve before this is over with.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: We'll have a conversation with her.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Since 1901, Charlotte Pipe has been a family-owned American manufacturer of high-quality pipe and fittings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: We're one of the nation's largest manufacturers of cast iron and plastic pipe and fittings, and we have extensive experience with both materials and an unwavering commitment to safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: I've traveled New York City today to express our opposition to the block-by-block proposal to expand the use of plastic pipe in buildings taller than five stories.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: These and similar restrictions exist nationwide due to the longstanding safety concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: With more of a century of experience in manufacturing cast iron and plastic piping, Charlotte Pipe is in a unique position to speak on the risks of expanding plastic piping in large residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Fire safety is the primary concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: In buildings taller than five stories, evacuating residents can take more time, making fire protection especially critical.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Plastic piping can melt, burn, and generate harmful gases during a fire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: As you heard earlier, these systems rely completely on fire-stopping devices between wall and floor penetrations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Once concealed, these devices can be difficult to inspect, maintain, creating additional concerns for building safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: As well, these fire stopping manufacturers do

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: do not warranty the performance of these products.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: for the life of their buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: So I think it's important for the council to understand that height restrictions, they're not uncommon in the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Lots of states have height restrictions, and we would urge the council to not expand the existing height restrictions in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Biggers
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: Chair Riley, I appreciate earlier you had voiced concern about the number of units of affordable housing seeming to be

utterances.text: like the number one goal and actually being concerned about the effectiveness or implementation rather than just chasing a number.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kyle Ems

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kyle Ems
utterances.text: It costs the city of over a third of a billion dollars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kyle Ems

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kyle Ems
utterances.text: No tenants want it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kyle Ems

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kyle Ems
utterances.text: No one is dissenting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kyle Ems

chapters.summary: He supports accelerating affordable housing, but says asbestos permitting delays are a critical obstacle, and urges support for professional certification legislation to speed up abatement.
chapters.title: Fabian Derewiecki of Local 78 testifies on asbestos permitting delays

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Good afternoon for the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: This is my son's first name.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: So good afternoon, Chair Riley and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today on Mayor Mandani's block by block housing plan and the importance of removing barriers to affordable housing construction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: My name is Fabian Derwiski and I'm here on behalf of Local 78, the Asbestos, Lead and Hazardous Waste Laborers Union.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Our members perform hazardous materials remediation, including asbestos, lead, and mold removal at the construction sites throughout New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: We support efforts to accelerate affordable housing development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: From our perspective, one critical obstacle must be addressed, delays in asbestos permitting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Asbestos abatement is often among the first steps in construction project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: When approvals are delayed, the entire project is delayed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: The city has a strong regulatory framework throughout the Department of Environmental Protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Asbestos control program, which is overseen by the Asbestos Technical Review Unit, A3.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: However, due to staffing shortages, approvals that once took weeks are now taking months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: This can leave office to residential conversions and other types of housing stalled before construction even begins.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: This increases costs and delays the delivery of desperately needed housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: The block-by-block housing plan mentions this specific issue on page 100.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: These delays also have serious safety implications.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: As a union, job site safety for our members and other trades is our priority.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: However, when asbestos remains in place on the job site, it puts workers at risk of exposure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: The slowness of DEP's approval is not making construction safer, it is making it more dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Allowing professional certification or ProCert would speed up the removal of asbestos so fewer workers are at risk of exposure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Local 78 has been working with Councilmember Riley on legislation to allow qualified professionals to use professional certification in the asbestos permitting process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: This would allow qualified professionals to certify

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: compliant plans and proceed with abatement without waiting months for DEP approval.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: The block-by-block housing plan seeks to accelerate affordable housing development in a safe manner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: To achieve this goal, the city must address the permitting delays that prevent projects from advancing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: We urge the council to support the process legislation when introduced and work toward its prompt passage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Our members are ready to do work necessary.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Your time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: And to bring affordable housing to New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Fabian Derewiecki
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: Committee on Land Use held a vote on three land use proposals (Convent Avenue, Coney Island Avenue, Sapphire Street) and an oversight hearing on Mayor Mamdani's Block-by-Block housing plan.

Administration officials from DCP and HPD testified on the plan's goals, fast-track districts, and infrastructure concerns, facing extensive Q&A from council members about community engagement, affordability, and capital planning.

Public testimony included advocates, community board members, union representatives, and residents, with many calling for comprehensive planning, deeper affordability, and preservation of existing housing.
